text: The Patriots are gearing up for their Sunday home opener against the Steelers at 1 PM ET, but they'll be doing so without one of their key offensive weapons after A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 that will land him on injured reserve for at least four weeks—forcing the question of who steps up in his absence as Mike Reiss examines in his breakdown of training. Meanwhile, the team has made a flurry of roster moves to shore up depth: they've added defensive tackle DaQuan Jones on a one-year deal worth up to $6 million and signed rookie linebacker Xavier Holmes and first-year wide receiver Chandler Brayboy to the practice squad, though they've also released safety Elliott Davison and running back Hassan Haskins from the practice squad after Davison's brief re-signing. In other business, Patriots owner Robert Kraft made clear the organization's values by stating he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium performances, citing the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."
